title: A Colony for the Terminal
premise: Quentin Ravensworth smuggles stolen memories past orbital customs and keeps the beacon lit on a station no one will admit to funding. When the freighter Halcyon Return docks carrying a crew aged backward into childhood, Quentin realizes his contraband memories are fragments of a massacre Earth's archives have been rewritten to erase. As the transmission loop counting down to a total records purge ticks toward zero, Quentin must reunite the regressed crew with their own smuggled memories and broadcast proof before the beacon—and everyone who ever docked there—is quietly deleted. The massacre is proven, but only by sacrificing the station, the beacon, and Quentin's own stored identity.
about_author: Jonah Halloran is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator turned science fiction writer, known for novels about people who keep signals alive after everyone else has moved on. Halloran lives off-grid on a coastal headland and claims to answer letters only by shortwave.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Quentin Ravensworth runs his nightly smuggling route through orbital customs, hiding memory-chips in beacon maintenance parts. His POV establishes the lonely rhythm of the station and the transmission loop ticking in the background. Emotional beat: competent isolation masking a fear that he, too, could be edited out of existence.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: A client pays Quentin to smuggle a sealed memory core labeled with coordinates he recognizes as his own station. Through his POV we learn how memory-smuggling works and that some chips hum when he sleeps near them. Emotional beat: unease—the first crack in his belief that he's just a courier, not a participant.

chapters.title: Halcyon Return
chapters.summary: A deep-space freighter docks unannounced; its crew are all children wearing adult rank insignia. Customs wants them quarantined; Quentin, POV alternating briefly with the ship's child-captain Mara, hides them instead. Emotional beat: protective instinct overriding self-preservation.

chapters.title: Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Mara, mentally eight but speaking in fragments of a forty-year-old officer, describes a planet called Verity Station and something that happened there 'before the calendar was fixed.' Quentin cross-checks and finds no record Verity existed. Emotional beat: vertigo—reality itself feels negotiable.

chapters.title: Customs Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Inspector Ade Okafor arrives to audit the beacon's commissioning papers, which Quentin cannot produce because he never received any. His POV plays a cat-and-mouse inspection while the children hide in the memory vault. Emotional beat: claustrophobic tension and the first hint Okafor may not be what he seems.

chapters.title: The Vault Hums
chapters.summary: Quentin discovers the humming chips resonate with the children's presence—they are fragments of the crew's own excised memories. Mara touches one and briefly becomes an adult, naming the date of the Verity massacre. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Earth's Last Loop
chapters.summary: Quentin decodes the transmission loop: it isn't a routine signal but a countdown to a permanent archive purge, after which all pre-loop records become legally void. Okafor, POV chapter, reports to an unseen superior that 'the Verity problem' is resurfacing. Emotional beat: the stakes crystallize—proof has an expiration date.

chapters.title: Children of the Massacre
chapters.summary: The regressed crew, guided by chip-fragments, reconstructs fragments of the attack: Verity Station housed witnesses to an corporate atrocity, and the survivors were aged backward to make their testimony legally worthless. Mara's POV, oscillating between child terror and officer resolve. Emotional beat: grief for selves they can't fully remember being.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Okafor offers Quentin amnesty and a new identity if he surrenders the children and destroys the chips. Quentin, POV, nearly accepts—until he finds his own name in a Verity crew manifest he has no memory of joining. Emotional beat: betrayal by his own past.

chapters.title: Who Commissioned the Beacon
chapters.summary: Following the manifest, Quentin learns the beacon was built by Verity survivors as a dead-drop for evidence—a lighthouse for a truth no port would receive. He realizes maintaining it was never a job but an inherited duty someone wiped from him. Emotional beat: mourning for a self he can't recover.

chapters.title: The Inspector's Mask
chapters.summary: Mara, POV, catches Okafor uploading a scrub-pattern to the station's systems—he is the purge made flesh, editing reality in real time. A chase through the docking arms ends with Okafor escaping and half the memory vault corrupted. Emotional beat: desperate loss.

chapters.title: Salvage Run
chapters.summary: Quentin takes the Halcyon out on a suicide run to Verity's coordinates to find physical evidence the archive can't delete. The children crew the ship with instinctive competence that terrifies him. Emotional beat: fragile hope forged in motion.

chapters.title: Verity Station
chapters.summary: They find Verity hollowed and sterilized, but beneath the scrubbing lies a sealed memorial vault the erasers missed. Quentin's POV; touching its door triggers a flash of his own erased memories of the place. Emotional beat: homecoming to a horror.

chapters.title: The Memorial Vault
chapters.summary: Inside: recordings, remains, and a full log of the massacre—including footage of young Quentin as a Verity archivist who chose exile over complicity. Mara's POV as she watches her adult self seal the vault. Emotional beat: devastating recognition.

chapters.title: What the Erasers Took
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts the man he was versus the courier he became, tempted to leave the past buried and save only the children. A dying crewmate's recorded plea reframes survival as testimony. Emotional beat: the theme lands—memory is the price of survival, and he must pay it forward.

chapters.title: Pursuit
chapters.summary: Okafor's enforcement ships corner the Halcyon in Verity's debris field. Quentin uses smuggler tricks and the station's hidden beacon codes to slip the net, losing the shuttle bay and two evidence crates. Emotional beat: costly escape, ticking clock now under four days.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Problem
chapters.summary: Back at the colony station, they plan the broadcast—but every relay will be scrubbed unless it originates from the beacon itself, whose commissioning signature predates the purge and thus outranks it. Okafor, POV, realizes the same thing and moves to seize the station. Emotional beat: race against erasure.

chapters.title: Siege of the Colony
chapters.summary: Enforcement teams board; the regressed crew defends the memory vault using knowledge their adult selves installed like muscle memory. Quentin fights toward the beacon core. Emotional beat: children becoming soldiers, courage without cynicism.

chapters.title: Restoring the Crew
chapters.summary: In the vault, Quentin feeds the crew their complete memories back—an act that may kill adults already living in child bodies. Mara chooses restoration, and the officer returns mid-battle to take command. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Climax: with minutes left in the loop, Quentin broadcasts the Verity record through the beacon's original signature, forcing it onto every archive simultaneously before the purge fires. Okafor tries to kill the power; Mara holds him off; the loop ends with the truth already replicated beyond deletion. Emotional beat: triumphant desperation.

chapters.title: After the Purge
chapters.summary: The purge executes anyway, wiping the old archives—but the broadcast stands as the sole surviving record, legally unimpeachable. Investigations begin; corporations fall; Okafor vanishes into inquiry. Quentin, POV, watches the machinery of accountability grind awake. Emotional beat: exhausted vindication.

chapters.title: A Colony for the Terminal
chapters.summary: Resolution: the station is formally chartered as a memorial colony for the restored Verity crew. Quentin, having spent his own archived identity to authenticate the broadcast, begins recording new memories—one honest entry at a time. Final image: the beacon still burning, now commissioned by everyone. Emotional beat: quiet renewal.
